item.text:
**Bottom line:** yes, but only moderately and with important caveats. By 2024 the U.S. had a much stronger jobs/inflation/growth mix than the post-pandemic inflation spike Biden inherited, and IMF/reuters sources describe a soft landing rather than a broken economy. The main offsets are that debt and deficits stayed on an unsustainable path, and a lot of the disinflation came from the Fed, global oil prices, supply normalization, and labor-supply/productivity gains rather than White House control alone.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Employment Situation Summary | U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2024-05-03 | https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_05032024.htm | April payroll growth and 3.9% unemployment show the labor market was still strong in 2024, which supports a stronger trajectory than the crisis conditions Biden inherited. | 5B.10, 5B.9 |
| Positive | Consumer Price Index Summary | U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2024-07-11 | https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_07112024.htm | Inflation had eased to 3.0% year over year by June 2024, a major improvement from the 2022 inflation peak. | 5B.10, 5B.9 |
| Positive | Gross Domestic Product, Second Quarter 2024 (Advance Estimate) | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis | 2024-07-25 | https://www.bea.gov/news/2024/gross-domestic-product-second-quarter-2024-advance-estimate | Real GDP grew at a 2.8% annual rate in Q2 2024, indicating the economy remained on a solid expansion path. | 5B.10 |
| Positive | Yellen says US 'soft landing' underway, low inflation, wage growth to spur confidence | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-01-05 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/yellen-says-us-soft-landing-underway-low-inflation-wage-growth-to-spur-confidence-3268343 | Treasury’s top economist described the economy as undergoing a soft landing, with low inflation and rising wages, which is direct support for a better trajectory than the inherited one. | 5B.10, 5B.7 |
| Mixed | Analysis-Fed meeting, benign inflation keep soft landing hopes alive | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-13 | https://ca.investing.com/news/economy/analysisfed-meeting-benign-inflation-keep-soft-landing-hopes-alive-3456485 | Reuters said the soft landing was being helped by benign inflation and Fed progress, which supports the positive trajectory reading, but also shows the White House was not acting alone. | 5B.10, 5B.9 |
| Mixed | The Biden-versus-Trump economy: Who did better on inflation, jobs, gasoline prices and more? | PolitiFact | 2024-03-04 | https://www.politifact.com/article/2024/mar/04/Biden-Trump-economy-who-did-better/ | Biden had stronger job creation than Trump, but the article notes inflation easing was also driven by Fed hikes, lower oil prices, and China’s slowdown, which limits attribution to Biden. | 5B.10, 5B.7 |
| Positive / Mixed | United States of America: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2024 Article IV Mission | IMF | 2024-06-27 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/27/cs62724-united-states-concluding-statement-of-the-2024-article-iv | IMF said activity and employment exceeded expectations and disinflation had been less costly than feared, but warned the fiscal deficit was too large, public debt was above prudent levels, and trade/subsidy distortions were a risk. | 5B.10, 5B.9 |

| Positive | Joint Statement of Janet L. Yellen and Shalanda D. Young on Budget Results for Fiscal Year 2024 | U.S. Department of the Treasury | 2024-10-18 | https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2657 | Treasury and OMB said jobs were strong, inflation had returned near pre-pandemic levels, and the deficit had fallen substantially, which supports a stronger near-term trajectory than the one Biden inherited. | 5B.10, 5B.7 |
| Positive | Impact of Biden's economic agenda may be felt long after his presidency | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-07-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/impact-of-bidens-economic-agenda-may-be-felt-long-after-his-presidency-3529572 | Reuters reported broad gains and long-run effects from Biden-era industrial policy, suggesting the trajectory may persist beyond his term rather than evaporate quickly. | 5B.10, 5B.8 |

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on the outcome side, but weaker direct evidence on causation. The best sources separate “better trajectory” from “Biden deserves all the credit.”
- The main counterweight is fiscal: IMF says debt and deficits were still too high, so the economy was not left fully stabilized.
- The best evidence for external constraints is that disinflation was helped by the Fed, lower oil prices, China’s slowdown, higher productivity, and expanded labor supply. That means a lot of the improvement was real, but not purely policy-made.
- I did not find a 2024 source showing the economy was worse off at the end of Biden’s term than at the start; the strongest negative evidence is about incomplete fiscal repair, not a collapse in the macro trajectory.
